name: Rivendell
note: Fan work from Tolkien, whose work belongs to the Tolkien Estate; nothing from any book, film or game is used, and every shape here is this project's own geometry built from the description. The cleft, the moor above it, the Bruinen and the ford are generated by tools/make-rivendell.py. The point of the place is the ground: you come over open moor and it stops, and the valley is three hundred metres under your feet with the house on ledges partway down. Positions are [lat, lon] against an origin at the Last Homely House.

landmarks.name: The Last Homely House
landmarks.info: Not a palace and not a fortress: a long house of many halls on a ledge above the water, with the roofs pitched steep because this is a wet valley, the galleries facing the falls, and a fire going in it at every hour of the year. Everything about the building is about being somewhere else than the weather.

landmarks.name: The Hall of Fire
landmarks.info: The one room in the house that is never empty and never quiet: a hearth at each end, a floor for singing on, and the doors open onto the gallery over the river.

landmarks.name: The Bridge
landmarks.info: One span from the terraces to the west wall, with no parapet worth the name. There are several of these; this is the one everybody means.

landmarks.name: The Ford of Bruinen
landmarks.info: Where the East Road crosses. The water is shallow and quick over gravel, and the valley's defence is not a wall - it is that anything coming down the road has to stand in the river to get in.

landmarks.name: The falls
landmarks.info: Every stream on the moor arrives over the rim, and there are a great many streams. The noise of them is the reason nobody in the house speaks quietly.

life._: lanterns on every gallery, smoke from the hearths, mist off the falls, and leaves coming down the valley
